sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Digital Magazine Publishing and Sponsored Media Placements

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with hybridized Anglo-American commercial law practices)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA) – investment chapter, in force since 31 October 2012
Panama–Canada Free Trade Agreement – investment chapter, in force since 1 April 2013

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT framework, as amended by Law 70 of 2019); Decree 363 of 2015 (banking sector AML); Decree 262 of 2015 (non-financial professions); Law 254 of 30 November 2021 (National Beneficial Ownership Registry); Executive Decree No. 5 of 2022 (UBO registry implementing regulations); FATF 40 Recommendations, as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) appointing the Panamanian Resident Agent and Foundation Council members
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the founder's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) if the jurisdiction is a contracting state; otherwise consular legalization at a Panamanian Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of founder's passport (photograph page) and proof of current residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing government authority and local registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Spanish translation of the English-language Foundation Charter and Regulations (Escritura Constitutiva y Estatutos)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified Public Translator registered in Panama
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization before a Panamanian Notary (no apostille required if executed in Panama)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of funds declaration and bank reference letter for the Founder and initial endowment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer certification with signature; apostille only when the overseas bank issues a sworn statement requiring international use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Personalidad Jurídica) of the corporate founder, if the founder is a corporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the corporate founder's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence (EDD) on domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates per Law 23 of 2015; compulsory screening of the Founder, Foundation Council, and any authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, and Panamanian national lists; all screening evidence must be documented, retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship, and made available to the Superintendency of Banks and the Financial Analysis Unit (Unidad de Análisis Financiero - UAF).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Online Name Reservation System (Sistema de Reserva de Nombre), accessible via www.registropublico.gob.pa; in-person filing at the Public Registry offices, Sección de Fundaciones
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory Spanish-compatible Latin alphabet; the Foundation name must contain the word 'Fundación' or 'Foundation' as a distinctive legal identifier; non-Spanish names are accepted but must be accompanied by a Spanish translation when presented to the Registry; no Cyrillic, Arabic, or ideographic characters are permitted in the registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the reserved name is still required after the initial 30-day window, the applicant's licensed Panamanian attorney must file a renewal request with the Registry before expiry; one consecutive 30-day renewal is granted upon payment of the applicable tariff. Upon rejection, the attorney must file a written Recurso de Apelación with the Director General of the Registro Público within 5 business days of notification, arguing that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registration; the Director General must resolve within 10 business days. If the appeal is denied, a further Recurso de Juicio may be filed with the Third Chamber of the Corte Suprema de Justicia within 2 months. Expedited submission of an alternative name is the recommended commercial practice due to lower cost and faster issuance.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted. The Foundation must maintain a physical registered office in Panama consisting of the Resident Agent's licensed law office; the Foundation's actual editorial operations, servers, payment platforms, and personnel may be located entirely outside Panama. Use of a P.O. Box as the registered office is prohibited; shared office space operated by the Resident Agent is accepted. No municipal operating license (Aviso de Operación) is required because the digital magazine portal has no physical place of business in Panama.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 2–5% annual probability of unannounced inspection for a standard low-risk digital publishing Foundation; inspection concentration increases to 10–15% in cases involving litigation, OFAC screening hits, or UAF intelligence referrals. On-site inspections in practice target the Resident Agent's premises and records rather than the Foundation's foreign operations.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve for expedited name re-filing, courier, and registry search certificates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Público de Panamá and third-party service providers

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law), as amended by Ley No. 47 de 2013 and Ley No. 61 de 2015; complemented by Executive Decree No. 463 de 2015.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Private Interest Foundations Section (Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta de Fundación (Foundation Charter / Deed of Foundation) executed before a Panamanian Notary
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Law 25 of 1995. The Foundation Charter must declare an initial endowment (commonly US$10,000, nominally as low as US$100) that may remain subscribed but unpaid. No escrow account requirement exists under Panamanian foundation law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME]

Whereas the Foundation Charter was executed before a Panamanian Notary and filed for registration, the Foundation Council hereby resolves:

1. To ratify the Foundation Charter and accept the initial endowment of US$10,000 as subscribed by the Founder.
2. To adopt the registered office located at [address], Panama City, Republic of Panama.
3. To appoint [Name] as President and [Name] as Secretary of the Foundation Council.
4. To empower the President to open banking and payment processing accounts (Stripe, AdSense), execute contracts, and appoint a resident agent or professional advisers as required.

This Resolution is passed unanimously and is effective forthwith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of Resident Attorney and Foundation Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) — Electronic Name Reservation Portal administered through a licensed Panamanian attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a licensed Panamanian attorney to submit three proposed foundation names to the electronic name reservation system. Pay the reservation fee online and obtain the Certificado de Reserva de Nombre (Name Reservation Certificate) confirming the name is available and does not conflict with any existing foundation, corporation, or trademark.
required_dossiers: Three proposed foundation names in order of preference
Notarized copy of the founder's passport
Power of Attorney (Poder) granted to the resident attorney
Statement of purpose referencing ISIC 5813 digital publishing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the reservation is refused for similarity, submit the alternate reserved name immediately; re-filing is the cost-effective cure. A name-conflict decision may alternatively be appealed to the Director of the Public Registry within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación) before a Panamanian Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary of the Third Judicial Circuit, Panama City (Notaría Pública del Tercer Circuito Judicial)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Founder and the Foundation Council members attend — physically or by irrevocable power of attorney — for notarized signature of the Acta de Fundación. The deed must contain the foundation name, head office in Panama City, initial endowment, statement of purpose covering digital magazine publishing and sponsored media placements, Council composition, and the beneficial ownership declaration required under Law 23 of 2015. The notary authenticates the signatures and one certified copy is reserved for the Registry.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of Founder and Council members
Draft Foundation Charter prepared by the attorney
Power of Attorney if signing by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any defect in the deed is cured by execution of an Acta de Rectificación (rectification deed) before the same notary, without re-execution of the original charter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription of the Initial Endowment and Internal Bookkeeping
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council (internal governance; no government filing involved)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting of the Foundation Council, adopt the First Board Resolution, record the subscription of the US$10,000 initial endowment in the foundation ledger, and appoint the President and Secretary. The endowment may remain subscribed but unpaid; however, the ledger entry is mandatory for compliance with Law 25 of 1995 regarding foundation assets.
required_dossiers: Foundation ledger (Libro de Registro de Fundaciones)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Resolution is queried, adopt a supplementary unanimous written consent in lieu of a further meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) — Private Interest Foundations Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Acta de Fundación together with the registry application form and the attorney's authorization letter. Pay the inscription fee of approximately USD 250. The Registry examines the deed for compliance with the Foundation Law, assigns the foundation number, and issues the Certificado de Fundación (Foundation Certificate) recognizing legal personality upon inscription.
required_dossiers: Two additional plain copies of the deed
Proof of payment of inscription fees and stamp tax (timbre)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues reparos (objections), cure the noted irregularity within fifteen working days by filing a corrected deed or an explanatory brief; failure to cure causes lapse of the application, requiring re-filing with a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Notice (Aviso de Operación) and Occupancy Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of Panama (Alcaldía de Panamá) — Commercial License and Aviso de Operación desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Foundation Certificate and the notarized Aviso de Operación form to the Alcaldía. Pay the proportional annual municipal tax (approximately USD 100) based on declared capital. In parallel, obtain the fire safety inspection certificate from the Fire Department for the registered office after an inspection of the digital operations workspace.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal denials are cured by correcting the declared activity code to 'services — digital publishing' and paying the corrected fee; an administrative reconsideration is available within ten days, but voluntary re-filing is faster.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registry (RUC) and Fiscal Status Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) — Online Taxpayer Registration Portal (Sistema TATA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the RUC application for the Foundation, selecting the economic activity code 5813 (magazine publishing). Apply for e-invoicing authorization, register for territorial taxation (Panama taxes only Panamanian-source income), and submit the sworn declaration of commencement of operations to the DGI.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUC application is suspended, correct the attached documentation within ten working days by electronic rectification; a formal appeal may be filed with the Administrative Tax Court if the issue persists.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 5813 digital magazine publishing is outside the Panamanian industrial licensing regime; no manufacturing or industrial permit required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Business Notice) — annual operating permit issued by the Municipality of Panama for commercial services activity

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of Panama (Ministerio de Ambiente — MiAMBIENTE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III — Exempt (administrative registration only; no full Environmental Impact Assessment required for office-based digital publishing with no industrial emission sources)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC emission thresholds applicable. Office wastewater must comply with municipal sanitary sewer ordinances. Electronic waste (obsolete servers, computers, and devices) must be handled through a certified e-waste recycler under Law 33 of 2018 on comprehensive waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (Certificado de Seguridad Contra Incendios) from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá for the leased office; structural occupancy approval confirmed by the municipal building occupancy certificate; general workplace safety (lighting, ergonomics, electrical installations) per MITRADEL regulations, with employer insurance obligations registered with the Caja de Seguro Social.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); online e-Tax 2.0 portal at https://etax.mef.gob.pa. Ancillary registers: Registro Público de Panamá (foundation deed and foundation council registration), Caja de Seguro Social (payroll, if Panamanian staff are hired), and the Municipio of the registered office for the Aviso de Operación. Foreign digital service suppliers register through the DGI non-resident digital services module of e-Tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Execute the foundation deed (Acta de Fundación / endowment act) before a Panamanian notary through a licensed resident agent (abogado agente residente); the deed must declare the initial endowment — no statutory minimum amount exists, but B/.10,000 is standard for banking and commercial credibility and the metadata's minimum capital requirement is satisfied by such declaration. (2) Register the foundation with the Registro Público (Fundaciones section) to obtain the registration number and issued certificate. (3) Apply through the resident agent at DGI e-Tax for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes), attaching the registered deed, agent acceptance letter, and identity documents of the Foundation Council members. (4) Obtain the Aviso de Operación from the municipal treasury for any taxable activity physically conducted in Panama. (5) Activate the e-Tax account, obtain the digital signature (Firma Electrónica certified by the Autoridad Nacional para la Innovación Gubernamental), and enable electronic invoicing. (6) Non-resident owners/beneficiaries require no physical presence; a local fiscal representative is mandatory and the resident agent may serve in that capacity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope: The PIF is a hybrid legal entity (separate patrimony without shareholders) recognised for civil purposes; for Panamanian income tax it is a separate taxpayer only on Panama-source income. All foreign-source income — including digital advertising, subscription revenue collected abroad, and foreign bank interest — falls outside the territorial tax net and is exempt from ISR (the 25% corporate rate applies only to Panama-source profits). The PIF is not automatically tax-transparent domestically, but it has no mandatory income tax return if it derives no Panama-source income. Its only unavoidable national charge is the flat annual foundation tax of USD 300 (Law 25 of 1995 as amended, due 31 January; late-payment fine of USD 300). A PIF carrying on business in Panama (e.g., a local sales team selling ads to Panamanian advertisers) becomes subject to corporate ISR of 25% on that Panama-source income and must file annual returns; the endowment contribution is not taxed, and no net-wealth or municipal asset tax applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists in Panama. Relevant elections and mechanisms: (a) early voluntary ITBMS registration before exceeding the registration threshold; (b) election to use the Régimen Simplificado del ITBMS (simplified fixed monthly payment) for taxpayers with annual turnover not exceeding USD 36,000; (c) advance tax ruling (consulta tributaria) before the DGI or the Tribunal Administrativo Tributario to confirm the export character of digital services; (d) contractual design of the foundation deed (reservation of powers to the founder, beneficiary designation, protector appointment) that may influence foreign jurisdictions to classify the PIF as a tax-transparent trust — this is a drafting election rather than a domestic statutory check-the-box; (e) OECD Pillar Two: for MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million, the Income Inclusion Rule and Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax of 15% under Law 361 of 2024 may apply, but a standalone PIF falls outside that scope; (f) no Panamanian hybrid mismatch election is codified, but because the PIF is territorial and not subject to CFC rules, hybrid mismatch exposure is minimal.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — a single-stage VAT-type transfer tax governed by Código Fiscal Articles 1057-1081, Executive Decree 84 of 2005, and Law 37 of 2019 (digital services regime). Note: Law 361 of 2024 temporarily raised the headline rate to 9% from 1 January 2025 through 31 December 2025, scheduled to revert to 8% in 2026 and 7% in 2027, subject to pending constitutional challenge. The digital magazine portal supplying subscriptions to consumers in Panama and selling advertising to Panamanian advertisers performs taxable services in Panama; services rendered to non-residents are outside the scope.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD 36,000 (B/.36,000) of annual gross taxable turnover distinguishes the simplified small-taxpayer regime from the general ITBMS regime; in practice, DGI expects registration as soon as taxable activity commences in Panama. Foreign digital service providers must register under the non-resident digital supplier regime from the first Panamanian B2C transaction with no de minimis threshold; once registered, monthly ITBMS returns are due. If the portal sells only to foreign consumers and foreign advertisers and no Panamanian consumption occurs, no ITBMS registration is required under the territoriality rule.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Factura Electrónica de Venta) applies to all ITBMS-registered taxpayers through the DGI e-Tax platform. Issuance requires DGI-accredited software producing XML/CAdES files with a DGI-authorised folio and security code (digital stamp). The clearance model is prior validation / pre-numbering by DGI, with real-time reporting capability via DGI web services/API for the largest taxpayers; foreign digital services suppliers must issue a simplified electronic invoice or receipt for each Panamanian transaction. Fiscal printers remain permitted only for small taxpayers under the simplified regime; QR-coded invoices are required, and the DGI can suspend issuers that fail validation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the territoriality principle, the sale of digital magazines and advertising inventory qualifies for the 0% export rate if the service is effectively used and exploited outside Panama and the counterparty is a non-resident. The DGI applies a use-and-enjoyment test: the contract must be executed abroad, the service recipient must be located outside Panama (foreign tax ID or passport evidence), and payment must originate from abroad. Subscription bundles combined with Panamanian-targeted advertising should be contractually split and allocated; the export character of digital advertising can be evidenced by IP-geolocation reports, advertising platform dashboards, and foreign advertiser country billing profiles. Domestic support services (local editing, local bank accounts) do not destroy the export character if the service is consumed offshore.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) for any direct export of goods
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (non-negotiable copy)
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Remesa / SWIFT MT103 credit advice) proving receipt of foreign funds
Export sales contract and foreign customer residence certificate (foreign tax ID or passport copy)
For digital services: IP-geolocation and server access logs, plus Stripe/AdSense payout settlement statements identifying foreign counterparties
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panama does not impose a statutory FX repatriation deadline because the official currency is the US dollar (Balboa at par); 180 days is adopted as the documentary benchmark. Failure to evidence inward remittance within 180 days allows the DGI to reverse the zero-rating and re-characterise the sale as domestic, assessing ITBMS at the applicable rate plus a 10% monthly surcharge (capped at 50%) and 1% monthly interest. False zero-rating claims attract administrative fines of 20%-40% of the omitted tax (Código Fiscal Articles 758-759); fraudulent claims constituting tax evasion under Law 70 of 2019 are punishable by 3-5 years of imprisonment and fines of USD 10,000-50,000. The DGI has a 3-year statute of limitations for assessments, extended up to 6 years for non-filing and unlimited in fraud cases, and may pursue joint and several liability of the resident agent and Foundation Council members for reckless filings.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) as banking regulator; Banco Nacional de Panamá as fiscal agent; no central bank with monetary authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates under a fully dollarized economy; the US dollar is legal tender. There are no exchange controls on current or capital account transactions. Profits and dividends may be freely remitted abroad without conversion restrictions. However, banks apply their own compliance filters for source-of-funds verification and FATF-aligned AML checks. Corporate clients face no statutory convertibility hurdles, but must complete standard documentary KYC and beneficial-ownership disclosure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement exists; export proceeds may be retained in any currency and freely used. Banks may require the supporting commercial invoice, bill of lading, or customs declaration for regulatory reporting and suspicious-transaction threshold purposes, but there is no forced sale or mandatory conversion ratio.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. Offshore digital EMIs are not separately authorized in Panama and non-bank entities may not accept deposits or issue payment instruments without a license from the SBP. A PIF may use regulated Panamanian banks for local clearing and recognized international banks or licensed fintechs with interoperable IBAN/SWIFT rails for cross-border collection; however, unlicensed EMIs will be treated as high-risk counterparties and may be rejected for payment service provider access.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one officer or duly appointed legal representative is generally required for account opening at Panamanian banks. Remote opening is permitted only where the bank maintains an approved video-identification process and the client has an existing relationship with a correspondent bank or a recognized introducer; direct fully-remote onboarding for newly incorporated PIFs is commonly denied. Directors who reside outside Panama may execute powers of attorney before a Panamanian consul or apostilled notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction or sanctioned jurisdiction linkage in beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Clean source-of-wealth declarations, sworn affidavits of beneficial ownership, apostilled passport copies, utility/address proof, professional reference letters from an SBP-licensed bank or law firm, and transactional rationale for the digital magazine portal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial substance of the PIF receiving ad revenue and sponsor payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foundation charter, registered economic activity statement (ISIC 5813), active domain and platform contracts, executed digital advertising agreements, Stripe/AdSense payout statements, projected traffic analytics, and a physical or virtual office arrangement in Panama.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-velocity cross-border inflows from multiple sponsored-media counterparties without a documented billing framework
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standardized media placement agreements, invoicing workflow, service description records, vendor KYC files for each sponsor, content moderation and anti-fraud controls, and segregated escalating reporting for transactions above the USD 10,000 threshold.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the PIF must be routed through a Panamanian commercial bank wire account using SWIFT MT103 with a clear beneficiary statement, referencing the foundation charter and foundation ID. Since Panama imposes no statutory purpose-code regime, the remitter should provide the bank with an investment intent letter, board resolution, or capital contribution resolution identifying the funds as paid-in capital or initial foundation endowment. For SaaS/advertising revenue, inbound receivables may arrive directly via Stripe or AdSense from global PSPs, then be swept to the Panamanian operating account through standard USD clearing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and operational disbursements use USD-clearing rails through Fedwire for domestic US settlements, SWIFT MT103 for foreign wire transfers, and commercial letters of credit for structured media/procurement transactions. Panamanian banks issue LC advices or confirm external LCs through correspondent relationships with US money-center banks. The PIF should maintain at least two active banking relationships to avoid operational single point of failure during discretionary disbursement windows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Offshore USD/EUR or USD/GBP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed through a SBP-licensed broker or international counterparty
Cross-currency swaps denominated in USD against functional currencies of sponsor counterparties
OTC currency options for receipt-side multi-currency ad revenue hedging

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Return (Declaración Anual de Fundación de Interés Privado) confirming continued existence, registered address, directors, and foundation purpose
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Fundaciones (Public Registry of Panama, Foundations Section)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of the foundation deed date; filing window generally from 60 days before to 90 days after registration anniversary; final acceptance by the Public Registry typically requires renewal within the anniversary month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment of the annual franchise tax and failure to file the annual maintenance cause a daily or progressive surcharge; continued delinquency of more than one taxable term triggers administrative dissolution or strike-off from the Public Registry, after formal notice and a cure period

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax Payment and Filing (Pago y Declaración del Impuesto Anual de la Persona Jurídica)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (online portal SIME / T@PA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before 31 March of each calendar year for the preceding fiscal year; new entities prorated from incorporation date through 31 December and due the following 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge on unpaid franchise tax plus cumulative interest; filing after deadline additionally triggers a penalty of USD 100 or 1% per month of unpaid tax; unpaid tax for two consecutive fiscal years is cause for preventive cancellation of the foundation registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of the Annual Report of Economic Activity and Transfer Pricing Compliance Annex (Annex C), where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For foundations with taxable Panamanian-source income, fiscal year-end filing deadline of 30 June following year-end; for non-taxpayer foundations, a zero-income return may be required administratively in the same window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual income return is punishable by a minimum fine of USD 300; inaccuracies attract additional interest and penalties up to 200% of the tax omitted; persistent non-filing is an independent ground for DGI-forced cancellation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Treasury Tax on Identified Securities (Impuesto de Timbre over Shares/Fondos Patrimoniales), if the foundation issues or transfers bearer or registered participation interests
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment is generally made at the moment of issuance or transfer and reconciled annually; annual filing by the corporate agent supporting no taxable events due 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Stamp tax deficiency attracts a 50% surcharge plus 1.5% monthly interest; failure to file the annual zero-event reconciliation exposes the foundation to loss of good-standing certificate issuance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Good Standing Certificate and Registered Agent Renewal (endorsement of the resident agent) supporting Public Registry continuity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Good Standing/Personería section) through the licensed resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The resident agent's appointment is renewed annually on the anniversary of the foundation deed; the Public Registry can require physical endorsement on the electronically filed renewal by the end of the anniversary month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Lapse of the resident agent endorsement automatically suspends access to legal personality acts; the foundation cannot obtain a good-standing certificate and is exposed to removal from the Public Registry after 90 days of unresolved agent vacancy

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for private interest foundations in Panama unless (i) the foundation carries on commercial activities producing taxable Panamanian-source income, (ii) it falls under DGI large-taxpayer classification, (iii) it is consolidated by a parent subject to SEC or Panama Stock Exchange audit requirements, or (iv) a foundation council member or third-party beneficiary contractually requires an audited statement. For isolated administrative holdings and passive digital publishing income paid by offshore payment processors, no independent statutory audit is mandated; an accountant's review of the internal books is optional.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as enacted by the Colombian/Continental Accounting Standards Committee?—Actually for Panama, mandatory framework is 'Normas Internacionales de Información Financiera (NIIF/IFRS)' for banks, insurance and listed companies; unlisted foundations may use IFRS or simplified local accounting records (Libro de Inventarios, Diario y Mayor), but IFRS for SMEs is the accepted professional standard when an audit is performed.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Panama's Law 70 of 2019 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) requires each private interest foundation to file its ultimate beneficiary ownership information with the DGI RBF system within 30 days of creation and to certify or update the registry annually in the month of the foundation anniversary. The resident agent must obtain, keep, and submit beneficial ownership data for all shareholders/founders, foundation council members, and beneficiaries with 10% or more patrimonial rights. No transactional UBO confirmation is needed at each shareholding transfer; instead, a new RBF filing and a revised foundation register entry are required within 30 days after the transfer. Failure to file or update leads to a USD 50 to USD 500 per month fine, loss of good standing, and the residence agent is jointly liable.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members or Founders (Registro de Miembros/Fundadores)
Register of Foundation Council Members (Registro del Consejo de la Fundación)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de la Fundación)
Register of Beneficiary Owners required by Law 70 RBF, held with the resident agent
Accounting Records Ledger and Supporting Documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 650 - USD 1,400 per year for a Panama licensed resident agent and registered office with compliance/RBF handling; premium corporate provider with filing timeliness guarantee ranges from USD 1,000 to USD 1,800.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 - USD 3,500 for an accountant's review or an IFRS for SMEs compilation/audit of a low-transaction digital magazine intermediary holding entity; mandatory certified audit for a mid-size active foundation ranges USD 4,000 to USD 8,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% on net taxable income up to USD 1,500,000; 25% on net taxable income exceeding USD 1,500,000 per Law 76 of 2019.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial exemption yields a 0% effective Panamanian rate on foreign-source digital publishing revenue (AdSense/Stripe proceeds sourced outside Panama) for a Private Interest Foundation; no general statutory tax holiday applies to digital magazine publishing; the annual flat franchise fee of USD 300 is the only fixed annual cost for a purely passive PIF.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 04 (Form 04) - Declaracion Anual de Renta para Personas Juridicas; filed via the DGI T@-C electronic portal (e-Tax/SITT platform, dgi.gob.pa) with payment through authorized banks or the DGI online payment module.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within three months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year taxpayers must file no later than March 31 of the following year. A nil or fully exempt PIF must still submit Form 04 with a sworn declaration (Declaracion Jurada) evidencing the territorial exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income from digital magazine subscriptions, digital advertising, AdSense payouts, and sponsored media placements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Panama-source income only; online platform sales to Panamanian subscribers and advertising served to Panamanian users are Panama-source; foreign click-through and subscriber revenue is excluded from this box.
PIF territorial-scope filers must document foreign origin of AdSense and Stripe proceeds with platform payout reports, subscriber country logs, and contractual counterparty residency evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, editorial production costs, and direct content acquisition costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible only if supported by invoices and contracts; costs allocable to exempt foreign-source revenue are apportioned and reported in the corresponding exemption schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: hosting, licensing, editors' salaries, marketing, and administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim deductions against Panama-source revenue only; expenses attributable to foreign operations are segregated to prevent distortion of the territorial tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income computed as Box 1 minus Box 2 minus Box 3 minus Box 4.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF with exclusively foreign-source digital revenue should show zero net taxable income; a reconciliation note must be attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax computed at 15% on the first USD 1,500,000 of net taxable income and 25% on the excess.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities with no Panama-source income enter zero; resident PIFs with local advertising income apply the progressive bracket.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits and prepayments: quarterly direct payments (pago directo), ITBMS credits, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are unavailable for exempt foreign-source income; advanced payments made during the year are credited here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alternative minimum tax: the greater of 4.67% of taxable gross income or 2% of net equity, if it exceeds the Box 6 tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF with zero Panama-source gross income and minimal equity is exempt from the minimum tax; Panama-source digital publishers must compute and pay the minimum tax if higher.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refundable after credits and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Surplus prepayments may be carried forward; refund claims require DGI audit and clearance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Distribution schedule: dividends or PIF distributions to beneficiaries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PIF distributions out of documented foreign-source earnings are marked non-taxable under Law 25 of 1995; distributions of taxed Panama-source profits trigger the 5% dividend withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of the tax due per month or fraction of delay, capped at 25%; late payment interest at 10% per annum; minimum fine of approximately USD 50 for late nil returns; persistent non-filing triggers DGI collection proceedings, bank account embargo, tax blacklist inclusion, and suspension of the entity's RUC registration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 02 (Form 02) / Declaracion de Pago Directo y Retenciones; submitted through the same DGI T@-C e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Advance income tax installments due on May 31, August 31, November 30, and February 28 for calendar-year taxpayers; each installment equals 25% of the prior year's final income tax liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year final ISR liability used as the prepayment base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PIFs with zero prior-year tax remit zero quarterly installments but must still submit the declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly installment computed at 25% of prior-year tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Newly formed digital publishing entities may instead remit 2% of monthly gross Panama-source income as an alternative pago directo.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits applied and net amount remitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source AdSense revenue is excluded from the pago directo base under territoriality.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-remission of quarterly advances carries the same 5% monthly surcharge up to 25% plus 10% annual interest; underpayment of advances also triggers a 10% underpayment penalty on the shortfall at final settlement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% final withholding tax on dividends distributed out of profits already subjected to Panamanian corporate income tax; 10% final withholding tax on dividends distributed out of untaxed or exempt earnings, including foreign-source income of a standard corporation; 0% under the PIF special regime (Law 25 of 1995) for distributions of documented foreign-source assets and income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama maintains DTAs with Mexico, Luxembourg, UAE, Singapore, Qatar, South Korea, Netherlands, United Kingdom, France, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Portugal, Barbados, and others. Administrative protocol: (1) request the Certificado de Residencia Fiscal from the DGI through the e-Tax portal, which requires an active RUC, sworn declaration of no outstanding tax debts, and statement of economic substance; (2) submit the certified TRC to the foreign withholding agent before or at the moment of the income payment; (3) apply the reduced DTA rate (commonly 0%-10% for dividends, 0%-10% for interest, 5%-10% for royalties); (4) retain supporting contracts and substance documentation for the applicable limitation-on-benefits clause; certificates are generally issued within 5-15 business days and are valid for the tax year stated.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Panamanian withholding: 0% on interest paid to non-residents where the underlying capital is deployed abroad and the debt is not collateralized by Panama-source assets; 12.5% withholding on Panama-source royalty and technical-assistance payments to non-residents where the IP or service is economically exploited within Panama; 0% where the IP is exploited outside Panama. Treaty rates commonly reduce Panama-source royalties to 5%-10% and Panama-source interest to 0%-10%, conditioned on TRC submission and economic substance compliance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File are triggered when annual gross revenue equals or exceeds USD 1,000,000 or aggregate related-party transactions equal or exceed USD 2,500,000, per the 2022 implementing regulations of Law 198 of 2021; Country-by-Country reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue above USD 85,000,000; entities below the documentation threshold must still file the annual transfer pricing informational annex to Form 04.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (Law 254 of 2019, Decree 131 of 2020) apply to resident entities conducting relevant activities: IP holding, headquarters, distribution and service centers, financing, leasing, shipping, banking, and insurance. A digital magazine portal owning platform IP and earning AdSense/sponsored-media revenue may be classified as IP holding or distribution; the PIF must demonstrate substantive direction and management in Panama, physical premises, local qualified employees, and adequate operating expenditure. An annual economic substance declaration is due to the DGI within four months after fiscal year-end (calendar-year entities: April 30). Fully passive PIFs with no relevant activity file a nil/out-of-scope declaration with supporting analysis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A PIF operates a digital magazine generating Panama-source advertising revenue from Panamanian advertisers, routes the proceeds through a foreign Stripe/AdSense account, omits the income from Form 04, and falsely claims the territorial exemption for foreign-source revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI surcharge of 5% per month of late filing (max 25%), 10% per annum late payment interest, plus the alternative minimum tax recomputation; criminal tax fraud under the Penal Code carries imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and a fine equal to double the tax evaded; civil restitution of the full tax deficiency and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false sworn returns face personal criminal liability and can be indicted jointly; courts may pierce the corporate veil upon proof of fraud, rendering directors' personal bank accounts and assets subject to embargo; preventive travel bans may be imposed during criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The PIF holds the digital magazine's platform IP and receives AdSense and sponsored-media payouts, but maintains no physical office in Panama, employs no local staff, holds board meetings abroad, and fails to file the annual economic substance declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of USD 50,000 for the first ESR violation and up to USD 100,000 for repeated violations; deregistration and forced dissolution by the DGI and the Public Registry; cancellation of the RUC; the foundation is barred from banking relationships and contract enforcement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors ('aluminum directors') are personally liable for misleading ESR certifications; directors may be disqualified from serving on any Panamanian licensed entity, fined, and their assets attached for restitution of fees received.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering and Piracy-Linked Funds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The digital magazine portal distributes copyrighted content without authorization (ISIC 5813 piracy), and the resulting AdSense/Stripe payouts are layered through the PIF's Panamanian bank account using fabricated editorial invoices while the PIF presents no genuine publishing substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering predicate offense under Law 23 of 2015 and Penal Code Article 254: imprisonment of 5 to 12 years, fines up to USD 1,000,000; asset forfeiture and freezing under Law 115 of 2019 (extincion de dominio); financial and administrative sanctions by the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) of up to USD 1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve the fictitious invoicing face predicate-offense money laundering charges, personal asset confiscation, imprisonment of 5 to 12 years, and travel bans; civil joint and several liability for bank losses as well as clawback of bridge loans and distributions follows under the veil-piercing doctrine.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Backdating foundation board minutes, fabricating economic substance records, or submitting false RUC/sworn declarations to the DGI and Public Registry to simulate Panama management for a digital magazine that is in fact managed entirely abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penal Code falsification of private documents: imprisonment of 2 to 6 years; annulment of the challenged corporate resolutions; invalidation of tax filings; the DGI disallows all claimed exemptions and recharacterizes the foreign-source income as Panama-source taxable revenue, with a 150% tax adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally liable for the falsification; personal restitution orders cover evaded taxes and third-party losses; preventive detention and travel prohibitions may be ordered, and the director's professional license to act as a fiduciary or corporate director is revoked.
